title: Comparison: Election Commission vs State Election Commission

blocks.content: The State Election Commission is an independent constitutional body and is not subordinate to the Election Commission of India.

rows: Parliament, State Legislatures, President, and Vice-President

Independent State Body (Not subordinate to ECI)

items: ECI does NOT conduct elections for Panchayats and Municipalities; this responsibility lies exclusively with the SEC.
Despite being appointed by the Governor, the State Election Commissioner cannot be removed by the Governor; removal requires a parliamentary process identical to a High Court Judge.
Articles 243K (Panchayats) and 243ZA (Municipalities) were incorporated via the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is constituted under Article 324, whereas the State Election Commission (SEC) is created under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
ECI conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President of India.
SEC is solely responsible for preparing electoral rolls and conducting elections for local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities).
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor but can only be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of a High Court.
The SEC is an autonomous constitutional body and is not subordinate to the Election Commission of India.
